newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares inch higher, volume remains slim.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares inch higher, volume remains slim.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.6 percent on Monday but traders said the gains were likely to be short-lived as foreign investors were unlikely to return to the fledgling market for another month.

Foreigners, the key source of liquidity on the Ljubljana bourse, were put off by a law introduced in February, requiring them to set up custodian accounts with Slovenian banks if they wanted to trade in domestic securities. Since then the SBI index has dropped 19.7 percent.
"Domestically there is not enough money there to sustain current prices, therefore I think shares may fall by another 10 percent by the end of April, while volumes will remain low," one trader said.
Banks said on Monday that they now expect to open the first custodian accounts at the end of April instead of at the end of March.
"The delay is a result of operational procedures which took more time than expected," said Alenka Narad of the foreign investment division at Slovenia's largest bank Nova Ljubljanska banka.
Traders said while buying shares at current prices could prove profitable in the long run, no short-term gains were in sight.
"I cannot see any share that could escape the general downward trend in the next month," a broker said.
The blue-chip SBI index fimed 7.95 points to 1,329.19.
Issue A of drug company Lek had the highest turnover, down 1.3 percent to 25,740 tolars on volume of 790 shares.
Overall eight shares rose, seven fell, two were unchanged and nine were untraded. Turnover firmed to 67.4 million tolars from 64.6 million.
Ordinary shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the leading gainers, rising 6.28 percent to 14,890 on volume of 38 shares.
Issue C of drug firm Lek was the leading decliner, down 7.89 percent to 25,000 tolars on volume of 15 shares.
